stem: A 6-year-old child snores loudly, has witnessed apnoeas during sleep, and is excessively sleepy during the day. Which of the following is the most appropriate first-line treatment for paediatric obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) when adenotonsillar hypertrophy is present?
explanation: Paediatric OSA is most commonly due to adenotonsillar hypertrophy, and adenotonsillectomy is the usual first-line treatment when this is present. CPAP is generally reserved for persistent OSA, contraindications to surgery, or selected cases. Snoring alone does not equal OSA, and polysomnography is helpful but not required in every child.

optionExplanations.A: Snoring alone does not rule in or rule out OSA, and symptomatic OSA needs active treatment.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: adenotonsillectomy is the usual first-line treatment when adenotonsillar hypertrophy is the main cause.
optionExplanations.D: CPAP is not the usual first-line treatment in otherwise suitable children with adenotonsillar hypertrophy.

combinedRecord.question_text_html: Which of the following statements are true regarding Paediatric Obstructive Sleep Apnoea (OSA)?

options.label: A
options.text: Everyone who snores will have OSA
options.text_html: Everyone who snores will have OSA

options.label: B
options.text: Aside from adQenotonsillar hypertrophy, other causes of OSA in children include craniofacial anomalies, Down’s syndrome and cerebral palsy (and other causes of hypotonia)
options.text_html: Aside from adQenotonsillar hypertrophy, other causes of OSA in children include craniofacial anomalies, Down’s syndrome and cerebral palsy (and other causes of hypotonia)

options.label: C
options.text: Untreated OSA can have significant consequences in children including growth delay, behavioural problems such as attention deficit/hyperactivity disorders, enuresis and pulmonary hypertension
options.text_html: Untreated OSA can have significant consequences in children including growth delay, behavioural problems such as attention deficit/hyperactivity disorders, enuresis and pulmonary hypertension

options.label: D
options.text: Sleep studies (polysomnograms) are necessary in all children to diagnose sleep disturbed breathing and OSA
options.text_html: Sleep studies (polysomnograms) are necessary in all children to diagnose sleep disturbed breathing and OSA

options.label: E
options.text: CPAP (continuous positive airway pressure) is the recommended first line treatment for OSA in children
